Banchan / Heritage

Oi Muchim Spicy Cucumber Banchan

Oi muchim is cucumber's same-hour answer to kimchi: sliced, salted ten minutes to draw the water, tossed in a gochugaru-garlic dressing and on the table before the rice cools.

Korean · Easy · Serves 4–6 as banchan

Chapter 03 / 25 banchan recipes ↗

Behind the dish

A PLACE AT
the table.

Stream: heritage — the instant cucumber bowl. Oi muchim is cucumber's same-hour answer to kimchi: sliced, salted ten minutes to draw the water, tossed in a gochugaru-garlic dressing and on the table before the rice cools. It is the cold-crunch bowl the spicy records keep calling for — the site's M-records reach for it the way rich tables reach for cold anything — and it is the easiest banchan on this list. No ferment, no cook, one law: salt first, dress second.

The cucumbers and salt
The dressing

Set yourself up

Before you cook

  • The ten-minute salt is the dish. Toss the sliced cucumbers with the salt and let them weep 10 minutes; the slices bend slightly, the water that would flood your dressing leaves now instead. Pour that water off — do not rinse.
  • Whisk the dressing while they weep; it takes four of the ten minutes.

LET’S make it.

  1. 01
    The wept cucumbers, squeezed gently by the handful over the sink (one squeeze, not a wring — cucumber should stay crisp, not crushed), into the dressing bowl. Checkpoint — the slices are flexible but still snappy, and the bowl they leave behind holds a clear puddle — that puddle is the dilution you just prevented.
  2. 02
    Everything tossed together, taste immediately, and adjust — cucumber wants the dressing slightly stronger than the target bite, because it keeps watering for the next hour. Checkpoint — the eating test two minutes later: cold snap, sweet-heat, garlic hum, sesame finish — the fresh register of #B03's fermented cousin, and the perfect reset bite after gochujang pork (#M13) or lacquered galbi (#M04). Chef’s Note — oi muchim versus oi sobagi (#B03) is the whole kimchi spectrum in two bowls: the stuffed cucumber ferments a day and tastes deep; this one waits ten minutes and tastes bright. The same table often runs both in one summer week — the quick bowl on the weeknight, the ferment on the weekend — and the cucumber is the only vegetable in the banchan world that carries both ends that convincingly.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
Dressing washed out in an hourSkipped or shortened the saltThe full 10 minutes; pour off the wept water
Slices soft, no snapOver-squeezed or salted too longOne gentle squeeze; 10 minutes, not 30
Bland at the tableDressed to target, not past itCucumber dilutes — dress a notch strong
Too hot to eat beside spicy mainsGochugaru-heavy dressingHalf the gochugaru; the bowl is a coolant

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

  • Best within 2 hours, edible at a day refrigerated; this is the make-and-eat bowl.
  • Variations: thin-sliced onion folded in for sweetness; a splash of vinegar to walk it toward the cho-gochujang lane (#SA03); matchstick apple in the dressing for the picnic build.
